role.altitude: The casting director keeps judging performers, negotiating and running auditions; availability chasing, slot booking, deal memo typing and status overviews shrink.
skills_to_grow: Running availability, holds and audition slots in one casting system
role.ambitious_version: A casting director who sees more performers per role because booking and admin take a fraction of the time.

tasks.short: Pass the director's requests to agents, collect availability and holds, discuss actors with the director, relay decisions to agents and actors, and keep a casting status overview.

steps.what: Casting director prepares the director's requests for availability and role details: by mail today; on the casting system's request form after the change
Casting director checks each request before it goes: role details and dates match the director's request, and it goes to the right agent
Casting director sends the checked requests to the agents
Agents reply with their actors' availability and conditions
Casting director tracks availability, holds and options per actor in a spreadsheet
Casting director serves as liaison with the director: discusses actors, changes and concerns
Casting director relays decisions, feedback and releases to agents and actors by phone, and writes the written confirmations and releases from templates
Casting director checks each written confirmation or release before sending: actor, role, dates and decision match what the director decided
Casting director sends the checked confirmations and releases to the agents
Casting director writes a casting status overview for the director and producer

approvals.approved_version: The availability requests with role details and dates exactly as checked by the casting director in s1b, sent once from the casting system to the named agents; any change needs a new check.
Each written confirmation or release with actor, role, dates and decision exactly as checked by the casting director in s5b, sent once to that actor's agent; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Availability requests go to agents through request forms in the casting system ({OTHER}), and agents' replies land in the record per actor and role, so holds and options are not kept in a spreadsheet. The status overview for the director is a view on that record. Talking with the director and calling agents and actors stay with the casting director; standard written confirmations and releases start from templates; the casting director checks each one and sends it personally. Availability requests are checked before they go.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability lived in mail threads and a personal spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Casting systems take agent replies through forms and keep holds per actor.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping directors, actors and agents happy when plans change.
tasks.human_edge: Trust with agents that gets a busy actor to say yes.
tasks.altitude: Less time on chasing availability; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether agents answer faster through forms than by mail.

evidence.claim: Casting systems send availability requests to agents and keep replies and holds per actor and role.
Actors' availability and conditions are personal data used only for the production.

assumptions: Boundary: from the director's requests to agents informed and the status overview; contracts are outside.
Input contract for s3: agents answer through the request form with dates, conditions and hold status; fallback is the casting director entering mail replies.
Coverage: about 70% of agents use the form; the s3 saving is priced at that share.
Agents' time is supplier labour and about the same as a mail reply.
Talks with the director and calls keep their full time.
unknowns: How many agents and actors per production.
Whether agents accept a form instead of mail.

already_counted.description: Casting director checks agent replies in the record and enters mail replies.

incremental.description: Casting director keeps request forms and templates current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few agents use the form and most prefer the phone (s1 90, s3 80) (12.5); high: about 70% use the form as assumed (23.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Get the budget and terms range, negotiate contract agreements with performers and agents, write the deal memo, get it approved, send it, have the contract drafted and check it against the deal.

steps.what: Casting director agrees the fee budget and terms range per role with the producer
Casting director negotiates contract agreements with performers and agents: fee, dates, billing and options
Casting director writes the deal memo with the agreed terms
Producer reviews the final deal memo and approves it
Casting director checks the memo before it goes: it is the version the producer approved, with fee, dates, billing and options as agreed, to the right agent
Casting director sends the approved deal memo to the agent: by e-mail today, by one release from the casting system after the change
Business affairs drafts the performer contract from the deal memo
Casting director checks the contract against the deal memo and answers agents' queries on it

approvals.approved_version: The deal memo exactly as approved by the producer in s4 and checked by the casting director in s4b, sent once from the casting system to the performer's agent; any change to fee, dates or options needs a new approval and check.

tasks.design: Agreed terms are entered once in the casting record, and the deal memo is generated from them in the house template; after the producer approves the final version, the casting director checks it and releases exactly that memo to the agent once. Business affairs generates the standard performer contract from the same fields, and a field-by-field comparison shows any difference between contract and deal memo for the casting director to resolve. Negotiation stays with the casting director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Terms were typed into the deal memo and again into the contract, and differences were found by reading both.
tasks.enabler_now: Document generators fill memos and contracts from one record.
tasks.still_hard: The negotiation with agents and the producer's budget.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what an agent will settle for without losing the actor.
tasks.altitude: Less retyping; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: How many contract errors came from retyping.

evidence.claim: Document generators fill deal memos and contracts from the fields of one record.
Performer fees and terms often follow collective agreements with minimums; the rules are national.

assumptions: Boundary: from the terms range to the contract checked; signing and payment are outside.
Input contract for s3 and s6: agreed fee, dates, billing and options entered in the casting record by the casting director after each negotiation; fallback is typing the memo.
Contracts follow the company's own template; contracts on an agent's paper are read in full.
Negotiation and the producer's approval do not change; business affairs time is outside the casting director's savings.
unknowns: Share of contracts on the agent's paper.
research_questions: How many contract corrections are needed before and after?

already_counted.description: Casting director checks generated deal memos.
Casting director resolves flagged contract differences.

incremental.description: Casting director keeps the deal memo template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a few lead deals negotiated on the agent's paper, read in full (s3 80, s7 90) (9.0); high: many supporting roles on the house template (19.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design the audition or screen test, schedule slots with agents, send audition details, book room, camera and reader, run the auditions and organise recordings for the director.

steps.what: Casting director designs the screen tests or auditions: scenes, format, in person or self-tape, and approves the audition pack
Casting director arranges audition slots with agents and actors by mail and phone
Agents pick audition slots for their actors
Casting director checks the audition details before they go: scenes and details are the approved version, for this role, to the agent of a booked actor, watermarked
Casting director sends scenes and audition details to the agents of booked actors
Casting director arranges the audition room, camera operator and reader by phone
Casting director checks the bookings before confirming: room, crew, dates, times and rates match the audition schedule
Casting director confirms the checked bookings with the venue, camera operator and reader
Casting director runs the auditions and screen tests
Actors upload self-tapes to the casting system for their role
Casting director organises recorded auditions and self-tapes per role for the director

approvals.approved_version: The audition pack with scenes and details exactly as checked by the casting director in s3b, watermarked per recipient and sent once to the agent of each booked actor; any scene change needs a new check.
The bookings with room, camera operator, reader, dates, times and rates exactly as checked by the casting director in s5b, confirmed once to each of them; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: The casting system ({OTHER}) publishes audition slots that agents book for their actors, with about the effort of a mail reply, and sends the approved audition pack, watermarked per recipient, to each booked actor's agent. Recorded auditions and self-tapes upload straight into the system per role and actor for the director to review. Designing the audition, booking facilities and running it stay with the casting director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Slots were juggled by mail and phone, and self-tapes arrived as links in many mails.
tasks.enabler_now: Casting systems offer slot booking for agents and self-tape uploads per role.
tasks.still_hard: Designing an audition that shows what the role needs.
tasks.human_edge: Getting the best out of a nervous actor in the room.

ambition.what: More self-tape auditions for actors outside the city who could not travel for a first round.

tasks.altitude: The casting director sees more actors per role in the same week; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether agents prefer booking slots themselves.

evidence.claim: Casting systems let agents book audition slots and actors upload self-tapes per role.
Audition recordings show identifiable people and are personal data, kept only for the casting.

assumptions: Boundary: from designing the audition to recordings ready for the director; choosing the cast is outside.
Input contract for s4: the booked slot and agent from s3 and the pack approved in s1; fallback is mail.
Coverage: about 70% of agents book slots themselves; s2 is priced at that share and the rest are booked by the casting director.
Agents' booking time is supplier labour, shown in s3.
Running auditions and booking facilities keep their full time; booking has its own check and confirmation. Actors' self-tape uploads (s6b) are supplier time.
s4 is part of notifying agents and actors of auditions, which sibling task 27-2012.04:11024 covers; its saving is counted there, so s4 keeps its full time here.
unknowns: Share of first rounds by self-tape.
research_questions: How many more actors are seen per role?

already_counted.description: Casting director books slots for agents who do not use the system and resolves clashes.

incremental.description: Casting director sets up slots and the audition pack in the system per role.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few agents book slots themselves and most auditions are in person (s2 70, s7 70) (9.0); high: about 70% book themselves and many self-tapes (21.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write and post the role breakdown, receive submissions, review performer information such as photos, resumes, voice tapes and videos, and agree the audition shortlist with the director.

steps.what: Casting director writes the role breakdown from the template in the casting system
Casting director reads the breakdown before posting: role, playing age, dates and fee band match the script and the producer's terms, with no wording that shuts out groups
Casting director posts the checked breakdown to agents
Agents submit performers with photos, CVs, showreels and voice tapes
Casting director reviews performer information such as photos, resumes, voice tapes and videos to decide whom to audition
Casting director checks union membership listed with submissions
Casting director agrees the audition shortlist with the director

approvals.approved_version: The role breakdown exactly as checked by the casting director in s1b, posted once in the casting system to the agents chosen for this production; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Role breakdowns start from a template in the casting system ({OTHER}), and submissions can be filtered on facts the casting director sets (playing age range, languages, availability), with every submission still visible; no model ranks or scores performers. The system does not ask for union membership at selection, so that check is dropped. Looking at the material and agreeing the shortlist with the director stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Submissions arrived in many formats, and selection needed watching everything.
tasks.enabler_now: Casting systems collect submissions in one format with filterable facts.
tasks.still_hard: Judging talent from a photo and a reel is the task.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the unexpected actor for a part.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; the casting director looks at the same material in one place.

reach.learn: Whether filters hide actors the director would have picked.

evidence.claim: AI that filters or evaluates candidates, including for self-employment, is high-risk; ranking performers to audition fits, so the design uses no model ranking.
Trade union membership is special-category personal data that may be processed only on a narrow legal ground.

assumptions: Boundary: from the role breakdown to the audition shortlist; auditions are outside.
Input contract for s3: submissions through the casting system with photo, CV, reel and stated facts filled by agents; fallback is mail.
Union membership is not needed to decide whom to audition; where a collective agreement needs it, business affairs handles it at contract stage.
Filters only narrow the view; the casting director can see every submission and no performer is rejected by a rule alone.
Reviewing material and the director talk keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether a collective agreement in the country asks for membership status.
research_questions: Do filters change who reaches the shortlist?

already_counted.description: Casting director opens the unfiltered list to check that filters did not hide suitable performers.

incremental.description: Casting director sets filters per role.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a lead role with few, hand-picked submissions (s3 95) (6.9); high: an open call with many submissions (12.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
